direction: Calibrate the mid-route capacity-fill weight to avoid spatial teleportation and introduce a scale-invariant voluntary early-return-to-depot gate (returning depot when normalized Clarke-Wright saving is too small).

operations.target: voluntary early return gate (return depot when current_node != depot)
operations.mechanism: After selecting the best mid-route candidate j, compute its dimensionless normalized Clarke-Wright saving sigma(i,j) = (d(0,i) + d(0,j) - d(i,j)) / max(d(0,i) + d(0,j), 1e-12). If sigma(i,j) falls below a threshold tau (around 0.15 to 0.35), return depot early instead of crossing the depot with a partially depleted vehicle.

operations.target: mid-route capacity-fill weight and depot pull
operations.mechanism: Reduce the linear demand/rest_capacity weight from 0.30-0.40 (which overwhelmed d_cur/scale ~ 0.10 in Round 1) to a moderate range (0.05-0.18) or quadratic/modulated form, paired with moderate-to-strong depot pull (alpha_mid around 0.70-0.95) and verified sign convention (smaller score = better, larger radial/saving = better).

operations.target: explicit depot-start branch and strict coordinate scale invariance
operations.mechanism: Keep the decoupled current_node == depot branch (heavy-far / radial-load seed) and strictly dimensionless ratios so objective/scale is invariant across scales 0.01 to 1000.

preserve: Exact select_next_node signature, voluntary early return only when current_node != depot (never return depot when already at depot), feasibility, and strict scale invariance.
hypothesis: H-004: Calibrating beta_fill <= 0.18 fixes Round 1's spatial teleportation regression, and adding a scale-invariant early-return gate on normalized saving sigma(i,j) < tau breaks the cross-depot bridge bottleneck and beats incumbent Frozen_C (-0.1089) across both dev and larger scales.

research_activity.question: Why did Round 1's scale-free decoupled candidates (-0.0615 best) lose to incumbent C (-0.1089), and can voluntary early return (return 0) break the ceiling?
research_activity.finding_summary: Code audit of Round 1 candidates revealed two concrete bugs: (1) candidates 1/2/4/5 used beta_fill=0.30-0.40 on fill=dem/rest_cap against d_cur/scale~0.08-0.12, causing 3x spatial teleportation when rest_cap drops; (2) candidate 2 inverted its depot-start sign and candidate 3 flipped the saving sign (+d_dep). Offline diagnostics also falsified naive terminal-stop +w_ret*d_dep penalties and 2-step lookahead (both hurt heavy stops). By contrast, a scale-free voluntary early-return rule returning depot when normalized saving sigma(i,j)=(d0i+d0j-dij)/(d0i+d0j)<tau (never used by A/B/C/V0) improved monotonically from tau=0 (-0.0939 dev, 18.80 multi-scale) to tau=0.25 (-0.1200 dev, beating C -0.1089 on all 4 instances, and 18.535 across 72 multi-scale instances).
research_activity.decision_summary: Keep the decoupled depot-start and strict scale invariance, tighten the mid-route fill weight to 0.05-0.18 with alpha_mid in 0.70-0.95, and add a scale-invariant early-return check (return depot only when current_node != depot and normalized saving sigma(i,j) < tau in [0.15, 0.35], possibly conditioned on partial vehicle fill). Do not add +d_dep penalties on terminal stops.
